It does not include National Insurance, student loan repayments, pension contributions, Marriage Allowance or Blind Person's Allowance. Check your tax code and payslips in your HMRC online account.
page.quickAnswer: For 2026/27 the first £12,570 of income is tax-free. In England, Wales and Northern Ireland you then pay 20% on the next £37,700, 40% up to £125,140 and 45% above that. Scotland has six bands from 19% to 48%. Above £100,000 your tax-free allowance shrinks by £1 for every £2 you earn, which creates an effective 60% rate between £100,000 and £125,140.

commonMistakes.title: Reading the bands as salary bands
commonMistakes.description: HMRC's bands apply to income after your Personal Allowance. The basic rate covers the first £37,700 above the allowance, which is £12,571 to £50,270 of salary for most people.

commonMistakes.title: Ignoring the £100,000 taper
commonMistakes.description: Between £100,000 and £125,140 each extra £2 of income removes £1 of allowance, so that slice is effectively taxed at 60% in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

commonMistakes.title: Mixing up Income Tax and National Insurance
commonMistakes.description: National Insurance is a separate deduction on your payslip with its own thresholds, and it is not included here.

faqs.q: How much can I earn before paying Income Tax in 2026/27?
faqs.a: £12,570, the standard Personal Allowance, if your income is £100,000 or less. Above £100,000 the allowance falls by £1 for every £2 of income and disappears at £125,140.

Between £100,000 and £125,140, each £1 of extra income is taxed at 40% and also removes 50p of tax-free allowance, which is then taxed at 40% too. Together that is an effective 60% marginal rate, plus National Insurance.
Yes. If you live in Scotland your salary is taxed at Scottish rates: 19%, 20%, 21%, 42%, 45% and 48% across six bands. Savings and dividend income use UK rates.

faqs.q: Why is my payslip tax different?
faqs.a: PAYE uses your tax code, which can include benefits in kind, underpaid tax from earlier years or a different allowance. Check your tax code in your HMRC online account.

sections.heading: How Income Tax on a UK salary works
paragraphs: The UK tax year runs from 6 April to 5 April. Employers deduct Income Tax through PAYE each payday using your tax code, which for most people is 1257L (S1257L in Scotland), the code for the £12,570 Personal Allowance.

Income Tax is charged on income above your Personal Allowance in bands. HMRC publishes the bands as income after allowances: in England, Wales and Northern Ireland the first £37,700 is taxed at 20%, income up to £125,140 at 40%, and anything above at 45%.
list: Personal Allowance taper: above £100,000 the allowance falls by £1 for every £2 of adjusted net income.
Scotland: six bands set by the Scottish Parliament apply to wages and pensions of Scottish taxpayers.
Not included: National Insurance, student loans and pension contributions, which also come off your payslip.

sections.heading: From Income Tax to take-home pay
paragraphs: The take-home figure here is your salary minus Income Tax only. Your real payslip will also show employee National Insurance and, if they apply to you, student loan repayments and workplace pension contributions.

Paying into a pension through salary sacrifice, or making gross pension contributions, lowers your adjusted net income. Near £100,000 that can restore part of your Personal Allowance, which is why many people in the taper zone increase pension contributions.
